```{r  data generation, echo = FALSE, results = "hide", warning=FALSE}
library(exams)

conc_hcl <- round(sample(seq(from=0.02, to= 0.98,by=0.02),1),2)
conc_h2so4 <- round(sample(seq(from=0.02, to= 0.98,by=0.02),1),2)
conc_koh <- round(sample(seq(from=0.02, to= 0.98,by=0.02),1),2)
conc_caoh2 <- round(sample(seq(from=0.02, to= 0.98,by=0.02),1),2)

sol1 <- round(-log10(conc_hcl),2) 
sol2 <- round(-log10(2*conc_h2so4),2)
pOH_koh <- round((-log10(conc_koh)),2)
pOH_caoh2 <- round((-log10(2*conc_caoh2)),2) 
sol3 <- round(14 - (-log10(conc_koh)),2) 
sol4 <- round(14 - (-log10(2*conc_caoh2)),2) 

# 14 = pH + pOH

```

Question
========
Calcular el pH de las siguientes soluciones acuosas (redondear el resultado a dos decimales):

Answerlist
----------

* $HCl$ $`r conc_hcl`$ M 

* $H_2SO_4$ $`r conc_h2so4`$ M 

* $KOH$ $`r conc_koh`$ M 

* $Ca(OH)_2$ $`r conc_caoh2`$ M 

Solution
========
Sabemos que $pH = -log(H^{+})$, $pOH = -log(OH^{-})$ y $14=pH+pOH$.


* Para $HCl$,  $pH = -log(`r conc_hcl`)$ = $`r sol1`$

* Para $H_2SO_4$,  $pH = -log(2*`r conc_h2so4`)$ = $`r sol2`$

* Para $KOH$, $pOH = -log(`r conc_koh`)=`r pOH_koh`$, $pH=14- pOH$, $pH = `r sol3`$

* Para $Ca(OH)_2$, $pOH = -log(2*`r conc_caoh2`) = `r pOH_caoh2`$, $pH=14- pOH$, $pH =`r sol4`$
